title: How a Sudden Mask Ruling Left the C.D.C. Reeling

sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 你好，我是安德鲁·罗斯·索尔金。

sentences.zh: 我为《纽约时报》的每日通讯《DealBook》报道商业和政策新闻。

sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: This is The Daily
sentences.zh: 这是《每日新闻》。

sentences.zh: 重大突发新闻。

sentences.en: The Biden administration now says the CDC's nationwide travel mask band-aid for airplanes and other forms of transportation is not in effect after a federal judge today
sentences.zh: 拜登政府现在表示，在一位联邦法官今天做出裁决后，美国疾控中心（CDC）针对飞机和其他交通工具的全国性口罩强制令已不再生效，

sentences.en: struck down the rule.
sentences.zh: 该裁决推翻了这项规定。

sentences.en: The unlikely story behind how an obscure lawsuit in Florida and a newly appointed judge ended the federal mask mandate on public transportation.
sentences.zh: 这背后是一个意想不到的故事：佛罗里达州的一起冷门诉讼和一位新任命的法官，是如何终结了公共交通领域的联邦口罩强制令的。

sentences.en: A huge shift in travel policy when it comes to the pandemic.
sentences.zh: 这是疫情期间旅行政策的一次巨大转变。

sentences.en: And why the case may endanger the federal government's legal powers to intervene in future public health crises.
sentences.zh: 以及为什么这起案件可能会危及联邦政府在未来公共卫生危机中进行干预的法律权力。

sentences.en: I spoke with my colleagues, Heather Murphy and Cheryl Gay-Stolberg.
sentences.zh: 我采访了我的同事希瑟·墨菲和谢丽尔·盖伊-斯托尔伯格。
zh_words: 谢丽尔·盖伊-斯托尔伯格

sentences.en: It's Tuesday, April 26th.
sentences.zh: 今天是4月26日，星期二。

sentences.en: Heather, I think for a lot of people, this legal ruling seemingly came out of nowhere and suddenly ended a centerpiece of President Biden's response to the pandemic.
sentences.zh: 希瑟，我想对很多人来说，这项法律裁决似乎是凭空出现的，突然终结了拜登总统应对疫情的核心举措。

sentences.en: But you have been reporting on the origins of this case.
sentences.zh: 但你一直在报道这起案件的起源。

sentences.en: So tell us what you found.
sentences.zh: 所以告诉我们你发现了什么。

sentences.en: Where does this start?
sentences.zh: 这一切是从哪里开始的？

sentences.en: This really starts in January of 2021.
sentences.zh: 这确实始于2021年1月。

sentences.en: I know the pandemic is such a blur.
sentences.zh: 我知道疫情期间的一切都很模糊。

sentences.en: It's hard to remember what things were like at that point.
sentences.zh: 很难记得当时的情况是什么样的。

sentences.en: But it's worth remembering that almost no one was vaccinated at that point.
sentences.zh: 但值得记住的是，当时几乎没有人接种疫苗。

sentences.en: And infections were really high, about 700,000 a day.
sentences.zh: 而且感染率非常高，每天约70万人。

sentences.en: And so Biden comes in to office.
sentences.zh: 所以拜登上任了。

sentences.en: And the first order I'm going to be signing here is relates to COVID.
sentences.zh: 我在这里签署的第一道行政令与新冠疫情有关。

sentences.en: And one of the first big moves he takes is he, along with the CDC, issues this executive order.
sentences.zh: 他采取的第一项重大举措之一，就是与CDC一起发布了这项行政令。

sentences.en: Mandating masks be worn, social distancing be kept on federal property and interstate commerce, etc.
sentences.zh: 要求在联邦财产和州际商业活动中佩戴口罩、保持社交距离等。

sentences.en: That says that masks are now going to be required in airports, on planes and in other forms of public transit.
sentences.zh: 这规定在机场、飞机和其他公共交通工具上必须佩戴口罩。

sentences.en: People start referring to this as the transportation mask mandate.
sentences.zh: 人们开始将其称为交通口罩强制令。

sentences.en: And really, when people were writing about it and talking about it, people were really attributing this to the White House.
sentences.zh: 实际上，当人们撰写和谈论它时，大家真的将其归咎于白宫。

sentences.en: This is the White House's move.
sentences.zh: 这是白宫的举动。

sentences.en: But what it really came down to was a very strong recommendation that was essentially an order from the CDC, the Centers for Disease Control.
sentences.zh: 但归根结底，这是一项非常强烈的建议，本质上是来自美国疾控中心（CDC）的一项命令。

sentences.en: And the reason they said that they were able to do this is because the federal government and the CDC have the ability to issue regulations that affect interstate travel
sentences.zh: 他们说之所以能这样做，是因为联邦政府和CDC有权发布影响州际旅行的法规，

sentences.en: when a disease is spreading between states.
sentences.zh: 当疾病在各州之间传播时。

sentences.en: Got it.
sentences.zh: 明白了。

sentences.en: And what was the reaction to this mandate?
sentences.zh: 那么对这项强制令的反应是什么？

sentences.en: Because I have to say, I don't remember it being issued.
sentences.zh: 因为我必须说，我不记得它发布时的情景。

sentences.en: And when a new president comes in, they issue a flurry of executive orders.
sentences.zh: 当新总统上任时，他们会发布一连串的行政令。

sentences.en: I didn't really remember this one.
sentences.zh: 我真的不记得这一条了。

sentences.en: So initially, I don't think there was a huge reaction because there were so many new mask rules emerging in all aspects of life.
sentences.zh: 所以起初，我认为没有太大的反应，因为生活中各个方面都在涌现出许多新的口罩规则。

sentences.en: And some airlines were already requiring people to wear masks.
sentences.zh: 而且一些航空公司已经要求人们佩戴口罩。

sentences.en: But gradually, it became more and more tense, particularly after people became vaccinated.
sentences.zh: 但渐渐地，情况变得越来越紧张，特别是在人们接种疫苗之后。

sentences.en: And masks became a huge battle point in the skies.
sentences.zh: 口罩成了航空旅行中的一个巨大争论点。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And then more recently, as some of these rules around masks began to fall away in other parts
sentences.zh: 然后最近，随着生活中其他领域的一些口罩规则开始消失，

sentences.en: of life, the airline industry, the travel industry, they began lobbying very hard for the White House
sentences.zh: 航空业和旅游业开始极力游说白宫

sentences.en: and the CDC to move this mask requirement for airlines and airports because they said they
sentences.zh: 和CDC取消这项针对航空公司和机场的口罩要求，因为他们说

sentences.en: weren't necessary now that people were vaccinated and that we were getting rid of mask requirements and other aspects of life.
sentences.zh: 既然人们已经接种了疫苗，而且我们正在取消生活其他方面的口罩要求，那么这些措施就不再必要了。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: And in the background, there's all these lawsuits, some by Republican lawmakers who are making a lot of noise about them, and some that really aren't on anyone's radar.
sentences.zh: 而在背景中，有各种各样的诉讼，一些是由共和党议员发起的，他们对此大肆宣扬，还有一些则根本没有引起任何人的注意。

sentences.en: And one of those lawsuits that very few people had any idea even existed was this lawsuit in Florida.
sentences.zh: 其中一起几乎没人知道其存在的诉讼，就是这起在佛罗里达州的诉讼。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: Tell me about this Florida lawsuit.
sentences.zh: 跟我说说这起佛罗里达州的诉讼。

sentences.en: Who are the plaintiffs?
sentences.zh: 原告是谁？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So this Florida lawsuit has three plaintiffs.
sentences.zh: 这起佛罗里达州的诉讼有三名原告。

sentences.en: The first is this woman, Anna Carolina Dassa, and she lives in the Tampa area, and she was hoping to visit her family in Columbia last AuguSt.
sentences.zh: 第一位是这位名叫安娜·卡罗琳娜·达萨的女士，她住在坦帕地区，她原本希望去年8月去哥伦比亚探望家人。

sentences.en: But her lawyer describes that she could imagine doing that if she had to wear a mask because
sentences.zh: 但她的律师描述说，如果她必须戴口罩，她无法想象能做到这一点，因为

sentences.en: she suffered from so much anxiety when wearing a mask, and she feels like she can't breathe, and it gives her panic attacks.
sentences.zh: 她戴口罩时会感到极度焦虑，觉得无法呼吸，还会引发恐慌发作。

sentences.en: And the second is this woman, Sarah Pope.
sentences.zh: 第二位是这位名叫莎拉·波普的女士。

sentences.en: And Sarah Pope also lives in the Tampa area, and she had a similar concern.
sentences.zh: 莎拉·波普也住在坦帕地区，她也有类似的担忧。

sentences.en: She couldn't go take a family trip to Hawaii, her lawyer writes, because the thought of wearing a mask for such a long flight gave her anxiety.
sentences.zh: 她的律师写道，她无法去夏威夷进行家庭旅行，因为想到要在这么长的飞行中戴口罩就让她感到焦虑。

sentences.en: And there's not a whole lot more explained about these two women in the complaint,
sentences.zh: 关于这两位女性，诉状中没有解释更多内容，

sentences.en: except that they both have anxiety when wearing masks, and anxiety is not recognized as a disability that you can get a mask exemption for.
sentences.zh: 除了她们在戴口罩时都会感到焦虑，而焦虑并不被视为可以获得口罩豁免的残疾。

sentences.en: And so they are arguing that they cannot fly and do the things they want to do because of the mask mandate.
sentences.zh: 因此，她们辩称，由于口罩强制令，她们无法飞行并做她们想做的事情。

sentences.en: Got it.
sentences.zh: 明白了。

sentences.en: And then we get to the third plaintiff.
sentences.zh: 然后我们谈谈第三位原告。

sentences.en: We are slipping ever closer to tyranny.
sentences.zh: 我们正越来越滑向暴政。

sentences.en: And the third plaintiff is not a traveler from Florida who doesn't want to wear a mask.
sentences.zh: 第三位原告不是不想戴口罩的佛罗里达州旅客。

sentences.en: The third plaintiff is this organization called the Health
sentences.zh: 第三位原告是这个名为“健康

sentences.en: Freedom Defense Fund, which is registered in Wyoming.
sentences.zh: 自由辩护基金”的组织，它在怀俄明州注册。

sentences.en: And it is actually run by this woman,
sentences.zh: 它实际上是由这位女士经营的，

sentences.en: Leslie Mnookian.
sentences.zh: 莱斯利·姆努基安。

sentences.en: This should frighten every American who cares about their freedom, our Constitution, and the future of our nation.
sentences.zh: 这应该会让每一个关心自由、宪法和国家未来的美国人感到恐惧。

sentences.en: And during the early stage of the pandemic, she founded this organization, which she writes is there to fight for what she calls bodily autonomy.
sentences.zh: 在疫情初期，她创立了这个组织，她写道，其目的是为了争取她所说的“身体自主权”。

sentences.en: Where does this stop?
sentences.zh: 这到什么时候才是个头？

sentences.en: Health Freedom Defense Fund is committing to defending our rights.
sentences.zh: 健康自由辩护基金致力于捍卫我们的权利。

sentences.en: And she created this organization to help put forward lawsuits against vaccine mandates and mask mandates across the entire country.
sentences.zh: 她创建这个组织是为了帮助在全国范围内针对疫苗强制令和口罩强制令提起诉讼。

sentences.en: The basic issue is that the federal government doesn't have the power to tell states or private businesses or anybody what to do.
sentences.zh: 基本问题是，联邦政府没有权力告诉各州、私营企业或任何人该做什么。

sentences.en: On her website, the organization makes a point that it urges people all across the country to join so that they can file lawsuits on behalf of them across the entire country.
sentences.zh: 在她的网站上，该组织强调呼吁全国各地的人们加入，以便他们可以代表他们在全国范围内提起诉讼。

sentences.en: And one of her first targets was the transportation mask mandate, which she found particularly egregious.
sentences.zh: 她的首要目标之一就是交通口罩强制令，她认为这尤其令人愤慨。

sentences.en: And her lawyers had the legal strategy to file this lawsuit in Florida, she said, and that she was connected to
sentences.zh: 她说，她的律师有在佛罗里达州提起这起诉讼的法律策略，而且她与

sentences.en: these two women with anxiety because they are members of her organization.
sentences.zh: 这两位患有焦虑症的女性有联系，因为她们是她组织的成员。

sentences.en: And do you understand why they thought it would be smart to file this lawsuit in Florida, of all places?
sentences.zh: 你明白为什么他们认为在佛罗里达州提起这起诉讼是明智之举吗？

sentences.en: So, you know, it's quite common actually to be strategic about where to file a lawsuit and to pick a district that seems most likely to be sympathetic ideologically.
sentences.zh: 你知道，实际上在提起诉讼的地点上采取策略，并选择一个在意识形态上看起来最可能产生共鸣的地区，是很常见的。

sentences.en: And so when her lawyers picked the Tampa area, they were picking a district that had a lot of conservative judges, including
sentences.zh: 所以当她的律师选择坦帕地区时，他们选择的是一个有很多保守派法官的地区，包括

sentences.en: judges who were put there by former President Trump explicitly with the idea of helping shrink the
sentences.zh: 由前总统特朗普任命的法官，他们的明确意图是帮助缩小

sentences.en: administrative state, meaning reeling back the regulatory powers of federal agencies.
sentences.zh: 行政国家，即收回联邦机构的监管权力。

sentences.en: That was actually a broader vision of that district.
sentences.zh: 这实际上是该地区更广泛的愿景。

sentences.en: So they were likely to get somebody sympathetic there.
sentences.zh: 所以他们很有可能在那里找到有共鸣的人。

sentences.en: And which judge ultimately is assigned this case?
sentences.zh: 那么最终是哪位法官被分配到了这个案件？

sentences.en: And what should we know about this judge?
sentences.zh: 关于这位法官我们应该了解什么？

sentences.en: So in terms of getting a judge, they lucked out.
sentences.zh: 在法官人选方面，他们很幸运。

sentences.en: Legal experts say they could not have gotten a better judge if they were looking for somebody to be sympathetic to their suit.
sentences.zh: 法律专家表示，如果他们想找一个对他们的诉讼表示同情的人，他们不可能找到更好的法官了。

sentences.en: The judge they got, her name is Catherine Kimball-Mizel, and she was appointed by former President Donald Trump.
sentences.zh: 他们得到的法官名叫凯瑟琳·金博尔-米泽尔，她是由前总统唐纳德·特朗普任命的。

sentences.en: She clerked with Clarence Thomas.
sentences.zh: 她曾担任克拉伦斯·托马斯的书记员。

sentences.en: She was part of the Federalist Society.
sentences.zh: 她是联邦党人学会的成员。

sentences.en: She has these impeccable conservative credentials.
sentences.zh: 她拥有无可挑剔的保守派资历。

sentences.en: A lot of people say she's also quite inexperienced, according to the Bar
sentences.zh: 很多人说，根据律师协会的说法，她也相当缺乏经验。

sentences.en: Association.
sentences.zh: 协会。

sentences.en: The American Bar Association rated her as not qualified to serve on the federal bench because of her lack of courtroom experience.
sentences.zh: 美国律师协会因她缺乏法庭经验，将她评为“不具备担任联邦法官资格”。

sentences.en: She was 33 at the time of her appointment.
sentences.zh: 她被任命时年仅33岁。

sentences.en: But nonetheless, she ends up with this case on her desk.
sentences.zh: 但尽管如此，她最终还是接手了这个案子。

sentences.en: And Heather, obviously this judge was ultimately sympathetic to these plaintiffs.
sentences.zh: 希瑟，显然这位法官最终对这些原告表示了同情。

sentences.en: We know that from the ruling she issues.
sentences.zh: 我们从她发布的裁决中知道了这一点。

sentences.en: But help us understand what her legal logic was in the ruling.
sentences.zh: 但请帮我们理解她在裁决中的法律逻辑是什么。

sentences.en: How did she arrive at the decision that President Biden's travel mask mandate should be struck down?
sentences.zh: 她是如何得出拜登总统的旅行口罩强制令应该被推翻这一结论的？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So it ended up involving the word sanitation.
sentences.zh: 这最终涉及到了“卫生”这个词。

sentences.en: And to just take a step back here, any judge who was going to evaluate the transportation mandate was going to look at the Public Health Service Act of 1944.
sentences.zh: 退一步说，任何评估交通强制令的法官都会查看1944年的《公共卫生服务法》。

sentences.en: That is a law that gives federal officials the ability to make and enforce regulations to prevent the introduction of a communicable disease from foreign countries and
sentences.zh: 这是一项赋予联邦官员制定和执行法规的法律，旨在防止外国传染病的传入和

sentences.en: inhibit its spread between states.
sentences.zh: 抑制其在各州之间的传播。

sentences.en: And so no matter what, any judge was going to take a look at that.
sentences.zh: 所以无论如何，任何法官都会审视这一点。

sentences.en: Got it.
sentences.zh: 明白了。

sentences.en: Because it sounds like that's the law upon which the mandate was based.
sentences.zh: 因为听起来这就是强制令所依据的法律。

sentences.en: Yes, exactly.
sentences.zh: 是的，完全正确。

sentences.en: And there is this kind of key line that becomes one of the focal points of her ruling.
sentences.zh: 而且有这样一行关键文字，成为了她裁决的焦点之一。

sentences.en: It says that these regulations could include inspection, fumigation, disinfection, sanitation, pest extermination, and then it says also in quotes, and other measures.
sentences.zh: 它说这些法规可以包括检查、熏蒸、消毒、卫生、害虫灭绝，然后它还说，引用原文，“以及其他措施”。

sentences.en: That the authorities judge may be necessary.
sentences.zh: 当局认为必要的措施。

sentences.en: And so there are some people in the public health law world who say, and other measures, basically gives an agency like the CDC the ability to
sentences.zh: 因此，公共卫生法界的一些人说，“以及其他措施”基本上赋予了像CDC这样的机构能力，去

sentences.en: introduce things that aren't explicitly covered in those different examples that they could not account for at the time of writing the law.
sentences.zh: 引入那些在撰写法律时无法预见、未明确涵盖在这些不同例子中的事物。

sentences.en: For example, masks.
sentences.zh: 例如，口罩。

sentences.en: For example, masks.
sentences.zh: 例如，口罩。

sentences.en: And there are still others in the public health sphere who say that sanitation actually covers masks.
sentences.zh: 公共卫生领域还有其他人认为，“卫生”实际上涵盖了口罩。

sentences.en: So a lot of people in public health see two different places within that sentence you just read to us where President Biden would have the legal rationale for a mask mandate.
sentences.zh: 所以公共卫生领域的许多人认为，在你刚才读给我们的那句话中，有两个不同的地方可以作为拜登总统实施口罩强制令的法律依据。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 正是如此。

sentences.en: But she's not interested in and other measures.
sentences.zh: 但她对“以及其他措施”不感兴趣。

sentences.en: She's focused on sanitation.
sentences.zh: 她专注于“卫生”。

sentences.en: And Judge
sentences.zh: 法官

sentences.en: Mizell chose to take a very narrow approach to interpreting the word sanitation, probably the most narrow approach a person could take.
sentences.zh: 米泽尔选择对“卫生”一词采取非常狭隘的解释，这可能是一个人能采取的最狭隘的方法。

sentences.en: She writes that sanitation refers to measures that clean something and wearing a mask cleans nothing, she concluded.
sentences.zh: 她写道，卫生指的是清洁某物的措施，而戴口罩什么也清洁不了，她总结道。

sentences.en: And therefore, along with some other different kinds of issues, she also takes with this whole rule, she concludes that the CDC, the federal
sentences.zh: 因此，连同她对整个规则持有的其他一些不同意见，她得出结论：CDC和联邦

sentences.en: government has overstepped its authority and that the Biden administration didn't have the authority to ever issue this mask mandate.
sentences.zh: 政府越权了，拜登政府根本没有权力发布这项口罩强制令。

sentences.en: Got it.
sentences.zh: 明白了。

sentences.en: And in that moment, the mask mandate is over.
sentences.zh: 就在那一刻，口罩强制令结束了。

sentences.en: It is.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: But people were very confused by this.
sentences.zh: 但人们对此感到非常困惑。

sentences.en: There are a lot of people pushing to end the mask mandate.
sentences.zh: 有很多人在推动结束口罩强制令。

sentences.en: There were thoughts that it might end very soon, but no one was expecting it to end that day.
sentences.zh: 人们认为它可能很快就会结束，但没人预料到它会在那天结束。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So I actually went to LaGuardia Airport in New York to try to see how it was playing out.
sentences.zh: 所以我去了纽约的拉瓜迪亚机场，想看看情况如何。

sentences.en: And I went up to travelers, all of whom were wearing masks, and none of them were even aware of this lawsuit.
sentences.zh: 我走近旅客，他们都戴着口罩，而且他们中没有人知道这起诉讼。

sentences.en: And when I went up to people at the desk who worked for the airlines, they also seemed confused about what exactly it meant for them at that point.
sentences.zh: 当我走到航空公司柜台前询问工作人员时，他们似乎也对这一裁决对他们意味着什么感到困惑。

sentences.en: It was really only later in the evening that all the airlines seemed to be on the same page.
sentences.zh: 直到那天晚上晚些时候，所有航空公司似乎才达成了一致。

sentences.en: This is the capital speaking.
sentences.zh: 这是来自首都的报道。

sentences.en: Also, for right now, you know, it's required a mask.
sentences.zh: 另外，目前来说，你知道，口罩仍然是强制要求的。

sentences.en: Woo!
sentences.zh: 呜！

sentences.en: Yeah, it's no optional for employees, passengers, following the White House.
sentences.zh: 是的，按照白宫的要求，员工和乘客都必须佩戴口罩，没有选择余地。

sentences.en: Woo!
sentences.zh: 呜！

sentences.en: And that's when you start to hear these stories of pilots mid-flight delivering information to travelers that they can take off their masks.
sentences.zh: 就在那时，你开始听到一些飞行中的飞行员告诉乘客他们可以摘下口罩的消息。

sentences.en: Oh my God, this is the best thing ever!
sentences.zh: 天哪，这真是太棒了！

sentences.en: And videos of people ripping them off and celebrating.
sentences.zh: 还有人们摘下口罩庆祝的视频。

sentences.en: You can follow them and wave them in the air like you just don't care.
sentences.zh: 你可以跟着他们一起，在空中挥舞口罩，就像你根本不在乎一样。

sentences.en: Woo!
sentences.zh: 呜！

sentences.en: We'll be coming here with your sex in just a moment.
sentences.zh: 我们稍后会为您带来相关报道。

sentences.en: And stories of other people feeling kind of freaked out that they got on a plane thinking that everyone would be wearing a mask and suddenly everyone's taking them off.
sentences.zh: 也有人感到非常惊慌，因为他们登机时以为每个人都会戴口罩，结果突然间大家都摘掉了。

sentences.en: The policy is changing, right?
sentences.zh: 政策正在改变，对吧？

sentences.en: Halfway through their journey.
sentences.zh: 在旅途中途。

sentences.en: Right, mid-flight, literally.
sentences.zh: 没错，真的是在飞行途中。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So this becomes one of those moments when a single judge applying her judgment and her analysis can really single-handedly change nationwide policy in a very big and dramatic way.
sentences.zh: 所以这成为了那种时刻，一位法官运用她的判断和分析，真的可以凭一己之力以一种非常重大且戏剧性的方式改变全国性的政策。

sentences.en: And in this case, in a matter of hours, based on her ruling, that mandate just evaporated.
sentences.zh: 在这种情况下，基于她的裁决，那项强制令在几个小时内就烟消云散了。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And everyone, the airlines, travelers, people who are celebrating, people who are feeling upset about this, are all asking themselves, what is the Biden administration going to do?
sentences.zh: 每个人，航空公司、旅客、庆祝的人、对此感到不安的人，都在问自己，拜登政府打算怎么做？

sentences.en: Are they going to fight this?
sentences.zh: 他们会反击吗？

sentences.en: Or are they just going to let this ruling be the final word on the mandate?
sentences.zh: 还是他们打算让这个裁决成为关于强制令的最终定论？

sentences.en: And that's it.
sentences.zh: 就是这样。

sentences.en: The transportation mask mandate is just a thing of the paSt.
sentences.zh: 交通口罩强制令已成为过去式。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: The New York Times app?
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》应用程序？

sentences.en: Unlocked?
sentences.zh: 解锁了？

sentences.en: Everyone knows you need to subscribe to the Times to access all of the reporting.
sentences.zh: 大家都知道，你需要订阅《时报》才能阅读所有报道。

sentences.en: But what if you could explore the Times for a month, for free, without putting in a credit card?
sentences.zh: 但如果你能免费试用《时报》一个月，而且无需输入信用卡信息呢？

sentences.en: Now you can.
sentences.zh: 现在你可以了。

sentences.en: When you download the New York Times app for the first time, your first month in the app is free.
sentences.zh: 当你第一次下载《纽约时报》应用程序时，你在应用里的第一个月是免费的。

sentences.en: A month to go behind the paywall to see what Times subscribers get every single day.
sentences.zh: 用一个月的时间突破付费墙，看看《时报》订阅者每天都能获得什么。

sentences.en: If you don't already subscribe to the New York Times, download the Times app today and get free access for 30 days.
sentences.zh: 如果你还没有订阅《纽约时报》，今天就下载《时报》应用程序，获得30天的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: Cheryl, our colleague Heather Murphy just told us that as this ruling comes down, the big question for everyone is what will the Biden administration do?
sentences.zh: 谢丽尔，我们的同事希瑟·墨菲刚刚告诉我们，随着这项裁决的下达，大家最关心的问题是拜登政府会怎么做？

sentences.en: So what is happening inside the White House when they learn about this ruling?
sentences.zh: 那么当白宫得知这一裁决时，内部发生了什么？

sentences.en: So inside the White House, there's a lot of confusion and a lot of disappointment.
sentences.zh: 在白宫内部，充满了困惑和失望。

sentences.en: The ruling really caught people off guard.
sentences.zh: 这项裁决确实让人们措手不及。

sentences.en: The CDC had just extended this mandate.
sentences.zh: 疾控中心刚刚才延长了这项强制令。

sentences.en: And now they had to scramble, along with the Justice Department, to figure out, you know, what were they going to do?
sentences.zh: 现在他们不得不和司法部一起匆忙应对，弄清楚他们到底该怎么办？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And the logical next step for any White House that puts into place an order like this and finds that a judge rules against it is to appeal it, right?
sentences.zh: 对于任何实施了此类命令却发现法官裁定其违法的白宫来说，合乎逻辑的下一步就是上诉，对吧？

sentences.en: You would think, but that's not what happened.
sentences.zh: 你可能会这么想，但事实并非如此。

sentences.en: So what does happen are a lot of internal deliberations, a lot of calls, discussions with the White House COVID response team,
sentences.zh: 所以发生的是大量的内部审议，大量的电话，与白宫新冠应对小组的讨论，

sentences.en: the CDC, some outside, you know, legal experts, the Justice Department about just what legal path the Biden administration can and should pursue.
sentences.zh: 还有疾控中心、一些外部法律专家以及司法部，都在讨论拜登政府能够且应该采取什么样的法律途径。

sentences.en: So that's what's going on on the inside.
sentences.zh: 这就是内部正在发生的事情。

sentences.en: But on the outside, there are all these conflicting messages.
sentences.zh: 但在外部，却充斥着各种相互矛盾的信息。

sentences.en: Josh, why don't you kick us off?
sentences.zh: 乔什，你来开个头吧？

sentences.en: Thanks, Jen.
sentences.zh: 谢谢，简。

sentences.en: Happy Monday.
sentences.zh: 周一快乐。

sentences.en: Jen Psaki, the White House press secretary, says at the briefing.
sentences.zh: 白宫新闻秘书简·普萨基在简报会上说。

sentences.en: So this is obviously a disappointing decision.
sentences.zh: 这显然是一个令人失望的决定。

sentences.en: The CDC continues recommending wearing a mask in public transit.
sentences.zh: 疾控中心继续建议在公共交通工具上佩戴口罩。

sentences.en: The CDC still recommends that people wear masks.
sentences.zh: 疾控中心仍然建议人们佩戴口罩。

sentences.en: And the CDC are reviewing the decision.
sentences.zh: 而且疾控中心正在审查这一决定。

sentences.en: But then the president takes a trip to New Hampshire and reporters ask him on the trip, you know, Mr. President.
sentences.zh: 但随后总统去新罕布什尔州旅行，记者在旅途中问他，你知道，总统先生。

sentences.en: People continue to wear masks on planes.
sentences.zh: 人们继续在飞机上佩戴口罩。

sentences.en: What should Americans do if they travel by plane?
sentences.zh: 如果美国人乘飞机旅行，他们应该怎么做？

sentences.en: Should they wear a mask?
sentences.zh: 他们应该戴口罩吗？

sentences.en: And Biden says.
sentences.zh: 拜登说。

sentences.en: That's up to them.
sentences.zh: 这由他们自己决定。

sentences.en: That's up to them.
sentences.zh: 这由他们自己决定。

sentences.en: Which doesn't sound like a president defending his federal mask mandate.
sentences.zh: 这听起来不像是一位总统在捍卫他的联邦口罩强制令。

sentences.en: No, it was very odd.
sentences.zh: 不，这非常奇怪。

sentences.en: People didn't know what to make of it.
sentences.zh: 人们不知道该怎么理解这一点。

sentences.en: But by that evening, the Justice Department announced that it would, in fact, appeal the court's ruling, but only if the CDC asked it to.
sentences.zh: 但到了那天晚上，司法部宣布，如果疾控中心提出要求，它确实会就法院的裁决提起上诉。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: Everything you're describing here is very confusing.
sentences.zh: 你描述的一切都非常令人困惑。

sentences.en: And as you said, a set of very mixed messages.
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，这是一系列非常混乱的信息。

sentences.en: So what exactly is going on here?
sentences.zh: 那么这里到底发生了什么？

sentences.en: Why does it seem like the White House can't quite decide whether to stand up for its own mask mandate?
sentences.zh: 为什么白宫似乎无法决定是否要捍卫自己的口罩强制令？

sentences.en: So there are a lot of complex legal and political considerations to this.
sentences.zh: 这其中有很多复杂的法律和政治考量。

sentences.en: And there's really two big questions.
sentences.zh: 实际上有两个大问题。

sentences.en: The first is, should they try to put this mask mandate back in place immediately?
sentences.zh: 第一个是，他们是否应该立即尝试恢复这项口罩强制令？

sentences.en: Should they appeal the judge's ruling so that they can get passengers on planes, trains, and buses wearing masks again?
sentences.zh: 他们是否应该对法官的裁决提起上诉，以便让飞机、火车和公共汽车上的乘客重新戴上口罩？

sentences.en: And that's complicated because the president has already said it's up to them.
sentences.zh: 这很复杂，因为总统已经说过这由他们自己决定。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: You have all these scenes of celebration, people taking their masks off and, you know, jubilation.
sentences.zh: 你看到了所有这些庆祝的场景，人们摘下口罩，你知道，欢呼雀跃。

sentences.en: And nobody wants to come in and be, you know,
sentences.zh: 没有人想跳出来成为那个，你知道，

sentences.en: the party pooper and have the Biden administration come in and ruin it by going back to court to try to get this mask mandate reinstated.
sentences.zh: 扫兴的人，让拜登政府介入并通过重回法庭试图恢复口罩强制令来破坏这一切。

sentences.en: But the other consideration is really an important long-term consideration, which is that if this judge's ruling stands, it could really tie the CDC's hands for the future,
sentences.zh: 但另一个考量是一个非常重要的长期考量，那就是如果这位法官的裁决成立，它可能会在未来真正束缚住疾控中心的手脚，

sentences.en: for all future pandemics.
sentences.zh: 针对所有未来的大流行病。

sentences.en: Explain that.
sentences.zh: 解释一下。

sentences.en: So this judge really went right to the heart of the CDC's core authority to protect the public health of Americans.
sentences.zh: 这位法官直接触及了疾控中心保护美国公众健康的核心权力。

sentences.en: Under the 1944 Public Health Services Act, the CDC had the legal authority to do what it did.
sentences.zh: 根据1944年的《公共卫生服务法》，疾控中心有法律权力做它所做的事情。

sentences.en: When it passed the law, Congress authorized the CDC to make and enforce regulations that, in its judgment, are, quote,
sentences.zh: 当国会通过该法案时，授权疾控中心制定并执行其认为，引用的话，

sentences.en: necessary to prevent the introduction, transmission, or spread of communicable disease.
sentences.zh: 对于防止传染病的引入、传播或扩散是必要的法规。

sentences.en: But, in essence, you know, the court said, no, the CDC does not have this authority.
sentences.zh: 但是，本质上，你知道，法院说，不，疾控中心没有这个权力。

sentences.en: So this was a serious consideration on the part of the White House.
sentences.zh: 所以这是白宫方面的一个严肃考量。

sentences.en: Did they want to let this stand and, you know, run the risk that it would become the law of the land?
sentences.zh: 他们是否想让这个裁决成立，并且，你知道，冒着它成为国家法律的风险？

sentences.en: It was very possible that if the White House took no action, then this was an existing federal court ruling and other courts might look to it to guide their own decisions.
sentences.zh: 很有可能，如果白宫不采取行动，那么这就是一个现有的联邦法院裁决，其他法院可能会参考它来指导自己的决定。

sentences.en: On the other hand, if the White House appealed and another court upheld this ruling, an appeals court upheld it, or even the Supreme Court upheld it,
sentences.zh: 另一方面，如果白宫上诉而另一个法院维持了这个裁决，上诉法院维持了它，甚至最高法院维持了它，

sentences.en: which could well happen given that the 11th Circuit Court of Appeals, the court that oversees the judge who issued this ruling,
sentences.zh: 这很有可能发生，考虑到第十一巡回上诉法院，也就是监督发布此裁决的法官的法院，

sentences.en: has a lot of Trump appointees, and we know that the Supreme Court now has a conservative majority, six to three.
sentences.zh: 有很多特朗普任命的法官，而且我们知道最高法院现在有六比三的保守派多数。

sentences.en: So if this ruling is upheld on appeal and upheld by the Supreme Court, then it definitely curbs the CDC's authority in the future.
sentences.zh: 所以如果这个裁决在上诉中被维持，并被最高法院维持，那么它肯定会限制疾控中心未来的权力。

sentences.en: So either way, there were risks.
sentences.zh: 所以无论哪种方式，都有风险。

sentences.en: There's risk whether you appeal or don't appeal.
sentences.zh: 无论你上诉还是不上诉，都有风险。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: There were, you might say, you know, no good decisions here.
sentences.zh: 你可以说，你知道，这里没有好的决定。

sentences.en: Damned if they do and damned if they don't.
sentences.zh: 左右为难。

sentences.en: So what does the White House decide to do?
sentences.zh: 那么白宫决定怎么做？

sentences.en: So this is a very sort of clever approach that they took.
sentences.zh: 他们采取了一种非常巧妙的方法。

sentences.en: Ordinarily, if you appeal a court's ruling, you would ask for the appeals court to issue a stay, to hold that ruling in abeyance, to set it aside until the appeal is settled.
sentences.zh: 通常情况下，如果你对法院的裁决提起上诉，你会要求上诉法院发布暂缓执行令，将该裁决搁置，在诉讼解决之前将其搁置一旁。

sentences.en: In other words, to allow the mandate to come back.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，允许强制令恢复。

sentences.en: Yes, exactly.
sentences.zh: 是的，完全正确。

sentences.en: But the Biden administration doesn't do that.
sentences.zh: 但拜登政府没有这样做。

sentences.en: So what they do is they appeal the ruling and they say, we're going to challenge this in court.
sentences.zh: 所以他们做的是对裁决提起上诉，并说，我们要在法庭上挑战这一点。

sentences.en: But they don't ask for a stay.
sentences.zh: 但他们没有要求暂缓执行。

sentences.en: And that means that they are abandoning this mask mandate.
sentences.zh: 这意味着他们放弃了这项口罩强制令。

sentences.en: This mask mandate is over and done with.
sentences.zh: 这项口罩强制令已经结束了。

sentences.en: And how do you interpret that decision?
sentences.zh: 你如何解读这个决定？

sentences.en: I think it was a very Solomonic decision in a way.
sentences.zh: 我认为这在某种程度上是一个非常所罗门式的决定。

sentences.en: They kind of split the baby, if you will.
sentences.zh: 他们算是各打五十大板，如果你愿意这么说的话。

sentences.en: It was smart.
sentences.zh: 这很聪明。

sentences.en: You know, they appealed.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他们上诉了。

sentences.en: So they sort of drew a red line and said, look, we don't want this federal judge to set policy for the whole country.
sentences.zh: 所以他们划出了一条红线，说，看，我们不希望这位联邦法官为整个国家制定政策。

sentences.en: We want to protect the CDC's authority as a regulatory agency.
sentences.zh: 我们想要保护疾控中心作为监管机构的权力。

sentences.en: But they decided to let slide the mask mandate itself, thereby eliminating the risk of another big public uproar over this very controversial policy.
sentences.zh: 但他们决定让口罩强制令本身失效，从而消除了因这项极具争议的政策而引发另一场大规模公众骚乱的风险。

sentences.en: So they're fighting for the principle.
sentences.zh: 所以他们是在为原则而战。

sentences.en: They're playing a long game here, is how I would say it.
sentences.zh: 他们是在下一盘大棋，我是这么说的。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: They're not worried about losing the battle, which in this case would be survival of the mask mandate.
sentences.zh: 他们不担心输掉这场战役，在这种情况下就是口罩强制令的存续。

sentences.en: They're more worried about losing the war, which is the long-term authority of the CDC to protect Americans in a public health crisis.
sentences.zh: 他们更担心输掉这场战争，也就是疾控中心在公共卫生危机中保护美国人的长期权力。

sentences.en: That's exactly right.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: In fact, that's how I've said it to colleagues, that they didn't want to win the battle and lose the war.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我就是这么对同事说的，他们不想赢了战役却输了战争。

sentences.en: So they abandoned the battle and focused on the war.
sentences.zh: 所以他们放弃了战役，专注于战争。

sentences.en: Cheryl, how good is the Biden administration's legal case here?
sentences.zh: 谢丽尔，拜登政府在这里的法律依据有多强？

sentences.en: Do they feel confident that they can win this larger legal argument that will preserve the authority of the CDC, the war, as it were?
sentences.zh: 他们是否有信心赢得这个更大的法律论点，从而维护疾控中心的权力，也就是所谓的战争？

sentences.en: Because the stakes of this are now very high.
sentences.zh: 因为这件事的利害关系现在非常高。

sentences.en: So I think they do feel confident.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为他们确实有信心。

sentences.en: One of the people that they have consulted, a public health law professor at Georgetown University, Larry Gostin, told me that they do have an extraordinarily good case on appeal.
sentences.zh: 他们咨询过的人之一，乔治城大学的公共卫生法教授拉里·戈斯汀告诉我，他们在上诉中确实有非常好的理由。

sentences.en: Heather already walked through the judge's ruling with respect to the word sanitation, and many legal experts, including Gostin,
sentences.zh: 希瑟已经梳理了法官关于“卫生”一词的裁决，许多法律专家，包括戈斯汀，

sentences.en: found that to be a very narrow interpretation that really fundamentally misunderstood the scope of the CDC's authority under the Public Health Services Act.
sentences.zh: 认为这是一个非常狭隘的解释，从根本上误解了疾控中心在《公共卫生服务法》下的权力范围。

sentences.en: But there's another part of the judge's ruling that maybe hasn't gotten as much public attention or doesn't go to the core of the CDC's responsibilities,
sentences.zh: 但法官的裁决中还有另一部分，也许没有得到那么多的公众关注，或者没有触及疾控中心职责的核心，

sentences.en: but something legal experts are seizing on, and that is that the judge faulted the CDC for failing to solicit public comment on the mask order,
sentences.zh: 但法律专家们正在抓住这一点，那就是法官指责疾控中心未能就口罩令征求公众意见，

sentences.en: saying that they violated this Administrative Procedures Act that requires public comment for most federal actions.
sentences.zh: 称他们违反了《行政程序法》，该法要求大多数联邦行动必须征求公众意见。

sentences.en: And legal experts say that in an emergency, federal agencies are exempt from that requirement, and that this pandemic most certainly qualified for an exemption.
sentences.zh: 法律专家表示，在紧急情况下，联邦机构可以豁免该要求，而这次大流行肯定符合豁免条件。

sentences.en: So they feel that that's another good ground for appeal.
sentences.zh: 所以他们认为这是上诉的另一个好理由。

sentences.en: Got it.
sentences.zh: 明白了。

sentences.en: So they believe pretty firmly that they will win a case that overturns this judge's finding that the CDC exceeded its authority.
sentences.zh: 所以他们相当坚定地认为，他们会赢得一场推翻这位法官关于疾控中心越权的裁定的官司。

sentences.en: I'm not sure I would go that far, but I think that they believe this is a risk worth taking, and that it's a risk that they have to take.
sentences.zh: 我不确定我会走那么远，但我认为他们相信这是一个值得冒的风险，而且这是一个他们必须冒的风险。

sentences.en: And so they are going to do everything they can to set this judge's ruling aside.
sentences.zh: 所以他们将尽一切努力撤销这位法官的裁决。

sentences.en: What's fascinating about this entire case, Cheryl, is that when this ruling was made,
sentences.zh: 谢丽尔，整个案件最迷人的地方在于，当这个裁决做出时，

sentences.en: I think it's safe to say we all thought it was a very big deal because it rewrote the rules for traveling in the middle of a pandemic.
sentences.zh: 我认为可以肯定地说，我们都认为这是一件大事，因为它重写了在大流行期间旅行的规则。

sentences.en: It suddenly meant lots of people might not be wearing masks, and that felt like a big deal.
sentences.zh: 这突然意味着很多人可能不会戴口罩了，这感觉像是一件大事。

sentences.en: But the reality is that its implications are much, much bigger than that,
sentences.zh: 但现实是，它的影响远不止于此，

sentences.en: because it may end up rewriting the powers of the federal government itself in any future public health crisis.
sentences.zh: 因为它最终可能会重写联邦政府在任何未来公共卫生危机中的权力。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's exactly right.
sentences.zh: 是的，完全正确。

sentences.en: I mean, it rewrote the rules of this pandemic,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，它重写了这场大流行的规则，

sentences.en: but we don't know what's coming in the weeks and months and years ahead.
sentences.zh: 但我们不知道未来几周、几个月甚至几年会发生什么。

sentences.en: Instead, we've already seen how many Americans have died from COVID-19 with the protections that the CDC has put in place.
sentences.zh: 相反，我们已经看到，即便在疾控中心采取了保护措施的情况下，仍有许多美国人死于新冠肺炎。

sentences.en: Imagine a similar virus with a CDC operating with its hands tied behind its back.
sentences.zh: 试想一下，如果一种类似的病毒出现，而疾控中心却束手束脚，那会怎样。

sentences.en: Well, Cheryl, thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 好的，谢丽尔，非常感谢你。

sentences.en: Thank you, Michael.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，迈克尔。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还需要了解的其他新闻。

sentences.en: After initially resisting his offer, Twitter has agreed to sell itself to Elon Musk, the CEO of Tesla and the world's richest man, for about $44 billion.
sentences.zh: 在最初拒绝了埃隆·马斯克的收购要约后，推特已同意以约440亿美元的价格将公司出售给这位特斯拉首席执行官、全球首富。

sentences.en: The sale puts control of Twitter in the hands of a frequent Twitter critic.
sentences.zh: 此次出售将推特的控制权交到了一个经常批评推特的人手中。

sentences.en: Musk has complained that Twitter's efforts at moderating content has veered towards censorship,
sentences.zh: 马斯克曾抱怨推特在内容审核方面的努力已经偏向于审查制度，

sentences.en: leading Twitter employees to ask whether Musk would reverse decisions like Twitter's permanent ban on Donald Trump for inciting violence on January 6th.
sentences.zh: 这导致推特员工纷纷质疑，马斯克是否会推翻推特此前的一些决定，比如因唐纳德·特朗普在1月6日煽动暴力而对其进行的永久封禁。

sentences.en: And We want to see Russia weakened to the degree that it can't do the kinds of things that it has done in invading Ukraine.
sentences.zh: 我们希望看到俄罗斯被削弱到无法再做出像入侵乌克兰那样的行径。

sentences.en: On Monday, during a visit to Poland, the U.S.
sentences.zh: 周一，在访问波兰期间，美国

sentences.en: Secretary of Defense, Lloyd Austin, toughened his message toward Russia, saying America's aim was not just to end the Russian invasion of Ukraine,
sentences.zh: 国防部长劳埃德·奥斯汀加强了对俄立场，称美国的目标不仅是结束俄罗斯对乌克兰的入侵，

sentences.en: but to degrade Russia's military capability so it could no longer carry out such missions in the future.
sentences.zh: 还要削弱俄罗斯的军事能力，使其未来无法再执行此类任务。

sentences.en: Standing next to Austin, Secretary of State Antony Blinken said that the U.S.
sentences.zh: 与奥斯汀并肩站立的国务卿安东尼·布林肯表示，美国

sentences.en: expected to quickly reopen its embassy in Kyiv, which was closed in the days before the invasion, a signal that the U.S.
sentences.zh: 预计将很快重新开放其驻基辅大使馆，该大使馆在入侵前几天关闭，此举释放了一个信号，即美国

sentences.en: thinks Russia is on the way toward losing the war.
sentences.zh: 认为俄罗斯正走向战败。

sentences.en: We're seeing that when it comes to Russia's war aims, Russia is failing, Ukraine is succeeding.
sentences.zh: 我们看到，就俄罗斯的战争目标而言，俄罗斯正在失败，而乌克兰正在取得成功。

sentences.en: Today's episode was produced by Stella Tan and Eric Krupke, and was edited by M.J.
sentences.zh: 今天的节目由斯特拉·谭和埃里克·克鲁普克制作，由M.J.

sentences.zh: 戴维斯-林恩和雷切尔·奎斯特编辑。

sentences.zh: 节目包含布拉德·费舍尔、丹·鲍威尔和玛丽安·洛萨诺的原创音乐，并由克里斯·伍德进行工程制作。

sentences.zh: 我们的主题音乐由Wonderly乐队的吉姆·布伦伯格和本·兰斯福德创作。

sentences.en: For decades, the Brooklyn Democratic Party operated as a tightly controlled machine.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，布鲁克林民主党一直像一台严密控制的机器一样运作。

sentences.en: Until this summer.
sentences.zh: 直到今年夏天。

sentences.en: When elections ushered in a bunch of self-described reformers.
sentences.zh: 当时选举迎来了一批自称改革派的人士。

sentences.en: Ever since, the party has been in the grip of a bruising, chaotic, and sometimes thrilling fight.
sentences.zh: 从那以后，该党一直陷入一场激烈、混乱，有时甚至令人兴奋的斗争之中。

sentences.en: In the latest episode of Metro, with me, Sarah Koenig, stories of people trying to maintain their influence and losing control along the way.
sentences.zh: 在最新一期的《地铁》节目中，我，莎拉·凯尼格，将讲述人们试图维持影响力却在过程中失去控制的故事。
